vessel.name: The ferry
vessel.description: A harbour ferry built as one long covered hall with two identical working ends, gates along both sides and benches across its width.
vessel.appearance: A low, even body with the same profile at both ends, one continuous roof, and a long band of sliding gates along each side; a small glazed helm cabin sits on the roof at mid-length, above a crew stair.

design_thesis.central_idea: The ferry is one long covered hall with two identical working ends. Each side opens along almost its full length through a row of sliding gates, so passengers board across the width all at once and the vessel departs in whichever direction its next pier lies. Closed, each gate sits flush between two posts; opened, it slides toward one end along a track just outside the hull plating and stacks behind its neighbour, leaving the side clear from post to post.
design_thesis.visible_difference: The vessel reads as a low, even body with the same profile at both ends, one continuous roof, and a long band of gates along each side. A small glazed helm cabin sits on the roof at mid-length, facing both ends, reached from the hall by a crew stair beneath it.
design_thesis.spatial_consequence: Benches run across the hall from one side to the other, so every seat lies a few steps from a gate on each side. The hall is one undivided space between two open sides, and its width, not its length, joins the seats to the pier.
design_thesis.coherence: The identical ends, the side gates and the cross benches all serve one rule: people move on and off across the ferry's width. Each depends on the other two, and together they turn a stop into a single movement of the whole crowd.

principal_dimensions.rationale: Length is set by how much of a waiting crowd must reach a gate at the same moment, so the hull is long enough for a full pier queue to board side by side. Beam is set by the cross benches and the standing space inside each row of gates, and ends where those bands end.

figures.note: Set by the length of a full pier queue.
figures.description: Length overall of the hull, inherited unchanged from the principal dimensions.

figures.note: Set by the cross benches and the standing bands.

construction.structure: The hall is one open span under the roof, carried by the posts along its port and starboard sides. Each side is framed as a row of openings with a post between each pair, so the roof loads pass down the posts around every gate opening into the hull side below.
construction.materials: A steel hull and steel posts, an aluminium roof, and glass in the upper half of every gate leaf and all round the helm cabin.
construction.block_division: The hull is framed from one template used at both ends; how the length between the ends is divided into blocks is not decided.
construction.assembly: The hull and the posts are built first, the gate leaves are hung and adjusted between the posts, and the aluminium roof is lifted on after them.
construction.weight_arrangement: The heaviest parts, the hull plating and the rudder and propeller under each square end, lie low and the same at both ends; the hall above is a light frame of posts under an aluminium roof, so the ferry trims the same whichever way it travels.

design_identity.novelty_thesis: A harbour ferry organised as one long covered hall that people enter and leave across its whole width, with no front and no back.
design_identity.conventional_patterns: Transformed: the single boarding door at one end becomes a full-length band of side gates. Rejected: the wheelhouse at one end, which gives a ferry a front.
design_identity.replacement_principle: People move on and off across the width, so the sides open along the hall, the ends are identical and the helm sits at mid-length facing both ends.
design_identity.superyacht_reading: It still reads at once as a harbour ferry: a low working hull carrying one long roofed passenger hall close to the pier, with the helm raised above it.

proportion_system.overall: Long and low: the hull is a little more than three times as long as it is wide, and the roof stands about one storey of headroom above the main deck.
proportion_system.masses: The hall runs almost the full length of the hull; the helm cabin is a small fraction of the hall's length and stands well under its own width above the roof.
proportion_system.vertical: The freeboard is the same short band at both ends and amidships. The hall rises about three times that band above the sheer, the helm cabin adds about half the hall's height again, and the draft is a little deeper than the freeboard.
proportion_system.signature_regions: The gate band takes nearly the whole side between the end bulwarks; the helm cabin is the only volume above the roof line.

global_silhouette.profile_view: A flat sheer with square ends of the same shape, one continuous roof line from end to end, and a small glazed lantern rising from the roof at mid-length.
global_silhouette.plan_view: Full width along almost the whole length, sides parallel from end to end and meeting each square end at a firm corner.
global_silhouette.silhouette_test: Without colour or fittings the outline is still symmetrical end for end, with the only raised volume at mid-length.

governing_lines.name: Sheer line
governing_lines.description: The sheer line runs level along the hull side from the forward square end to the aft square end; it sets the lower edge of the gate band and gives both ends the same profile.
governing_lines.line: A flat sheer running level along the hull side.
governing_lines.governs: The lower edge of the gate band and the identical profile of both ends.

governing_lines.name: Roof edge
governing_lines.description: The roof edge runs level over the Hall from the forward end bulwark to the aft end bulwark; it sets the upper edge of the gate band and draws the long horizontal of the silhouette.
governing_lines.line: The roof edge running level over the hall.
governing_lines.governs: The upper edge of the gate band and the long horizontal of the silhouette.

primary_masses.name: Hall
primary_masses.description: The Hall is the covered passenger body standing directly on the hull sides on the Main deck, running from near the forward end to near the aft end across the full beam and rising one storey of headroom above the main deck. Its posts rise straight from the hull plating, its ends stop at the raked end bulwarks, and it carries the roof and the Helm cabin.
primary_masses.role: The covered passenger hall standing on the hull.
primary_masses.position: On the main deck from near the forward end to near the aft end, full width.
primary_masses.relative_length: almost the full length of the hull
primary_masses.relative_height: one storey of headroom above the main deck
primary_masses.connections: Stands directly on the hull sides; carries the roof and the helm cabin.
primary_masses.transition_to_adjacent_geometry: Its posts rise straight from the hull plating, and its ends stop at the raked end bulwarks.

primary_masses.name: Helm cabin
primary_masses.description: The Helm cabin is the only volume above the roof: a short box, square in plan and well under the beam wide, standing on a low plinth on the roof of the Hall at mid-length on the centreline, its floor a step above the roof and glazed on all four sides. It is a small fraction of the hall's length and is reached from the Hall by the crew stair through a floor hatch.
primary_masses.role: The helm position, the only volume above the roof.
primary_masses.position: On the roof at mid-length on the centreline.
primary_masses.relative_length: a small fraction of the hall's length
primary_masses.relative_width: well under the beam, square in plan
primary_masses.relative_height: a short box with its floor a step above the roof
primary_masses.connections: Reached from the hall by the crew stair through a floor hatch.
primary_masses.transition_to_adjacent_geometry: Stands on the roof on a low plinth, glazed on all four sides.

primary_voids.name: Passenger hall interior
primary_voids.description: The Passenger hall interior fills the Hall on the Main deck from end to end across the full beam, bounded by the deck below, the roof above, the port and starboard gate bands at its sides and the end bulwarks fore and aft. It is enclosed, and opens to the pier along a whole side when the gates on that side open.
primary_voids.position: Inside m_hall on the main deck, end to end.
primary_voids.relative_extent: almost the full length and the full beam
primary_voids.boundaries: The hull deck below, the roof above, the gate bands port and starboard, the end bulwarks fore and aft.
primary_voids.relationship_to_surrounding_masses: Contained by the hall; opens to the pier along a whole side when the gates on that side open.

hull_geometry.stem_and_bow: Each end is square in plan and closes in a raked bulwark; there is no pointed stem.
hull_geometry.waterline_entry: Not defined beyond the square ends.
hull_geometry.freeboard_distribution: A short, even band of plating below the gate tracks along the whole length.
hull_geometry.midbody: Parallel sides along almost the whole length.
hull_geometry.hull_side_organization: Plain plating below the gate band, which carries the outer track.
hull_geometry.stern_and_transom: The aft end repeats the forward end exactly.
hull_geometry.hull_superstructure_relationship: The hall stands directly on the hull sides with no setback, so the gate band continues the hull side upward.
hull_geometry.design_waterline: Level from end to end, a short band of plating below the gate track at both square ends and amidships.
hull_geometry.underbody_and_appendages: A flat-bottomed hull with one rudder and one propeller under each square end; it has no keel fin, no bulb, no stabiliser fins and no thruster tunnels.

superstructure_geometry.primary_mass_organization: One hall body under one roof, with one small helm cabin on the roof.
superstructure_geometry.forward_to_aft_massing: Even from end to end, broken only by the helm cabin at mid-length.
superstructure_geometry.rooflines: One continuous level roof from end bulwark to end bulwark.
superstructure_geometry.setbacks_or_transitions: No setbacks; the hall sides are flush with the hull sides.
superstructure_geometry.relationship_to_hull: Integrated with the hull sides along their whole length.
superstructure_geometry.glazing_topology: The upper half of every gate leaf is glazed, forming one band along each side; the helm cabin is glazed on all four sides.

stern_geometry.aft_silhouette: The same square end and raked bulwark as the forward end.
stern_geometry.transom_closure: A square end closed by the raked bulwark.
stern_geometry.platform_terrace_or_recess_topology: None; the hall runs to the bulwark, nothing at either end moves and neither end has a way down to the water.
stern_geometry.relationship_to_waterline: The end stands at the same short freeboard as the sides.
stern_geometry.relationship_to_superstructure: The hall runs to the aft bulwark, which closes its aft end.
stern_geometry.forbidden_conventional_interpretations: A stern that differs from the bow, or a stern boarding platform.

bow_geometry.stem_type: Square end with a raked bulwark.
bow_geometry.rake_or_plumb: The bulwark rises a step above the main deck and rakes outward; the end itself is square.
bow_geometry.bow_volume: Full to the end, with the same width as the midbody.
bow_geometry.relationship_to_forward_superstructure: The hall runs to the forward bulwark, which closes its forward end.

signature_regions.description: Along almost the whole length of the port and starboard sides of the Hall on the Main deck, between the end bulwarks and under the roof edge, a row of sliding gate leaves fills the openings between slim posts, each leaf glazed in its upper half. Closed, every leaf sits flush with its posts, so each side reads as one glazed wall from end to end; the leaves run on an outer track just above the sheer.
signature_regions.visual_difference: A closed side reads as one continuous glazed wall; an open side leaves a clear run from pier to bench with no door frames.

topology.aft: ends at the aft end bulwark
topology.port: the port row forms the port side of the hall
topology.starboard: the starboard row forms the starboard side of the hall
topology.bottom: the outer track just above the sheer

signature_regions.relationships: Integrated with the hall sides and continuing the hull side upward.
signature_regions.must_preserve: One continuous band of leaves along each side, flush between the posts.
signature_regions.forbidden_interpretations: Separate doors in a solid side wall, or windows above a solid lower wall.
signature_regions.proof_conditions: One side shows a continuous row of glazed leaves from end bulwark to end bulwark.
signature_regions.verification: Weathertight seal of closed leaves in a seaway; locking of stacked leaves under wind load.

signature_regions.feature: Mid-length helm cabin facing both ends
signature_regions.description: The Helm cabin stands on the roof of the Hall at mid-length on the centreline: a low box, square in plan and glazed on all four sides, its floor a step above the roof and its flat top the highest point of the ferry. In profile it rises from the long roof line like a small lantern and looks the same from either end.
signature_regions.visual_difference: A small glazed box stands alone in the middle of the long roof instead of a wheelhouse at one end, so the ferry has no front or back.

topology.fore: the roof running forward to the forward end
topology.aft: the roof running aft to the aft end
topology.port: the roof walkway and the cabin door
topology.top: its flat top, the highest point of the ferry
topology.bottom: the roof, with a hatch over the crew stair

signature_regions.relationships: Above the hall at mid-length, the only volume above the roof line.
signature_regions.must_preserve: Mid-length, centreline, glazed all round, the same from either end.
signature_regions.forbidden_interpretations: A wheelhouse at one end, or a tall mast or funnel beside it.
signature_regions.proof_conditions: In profile the cabin stands exactly midway between the two identical ends.
signature_regions.verification: Sight lines to both ends over the roof.

signature_regions.feature: Folding boarding rail inside each opening
signature_regions.description: Inside each gate opening on the port and starboard sides of the Main deck, a waist-height rail spans between the opening's two posts, hinged on them above a recess in the deck edge, at the inner edge of the standing band just inside the closed gate leaves, so from outside it shows only through the glazing.
signature_regions.visual_difference: With the gates open the side still has a guard line while the ferry is underway, and nothing at all when it is boarding.

topology.aft: the post at the aft side of its opening
topology.port: the gate leaves on the port side
topology.starboard: the gate leaves on the starboard side
topology.bottom: a recess in the deck edge

signature_regions.relationships: Inside the gate band, hinged on the posts.
signature_regions.must_preserve: Raised in the standard state, visible only through the glazing.
signature_regions.forbidden_interpretations: A rail outside the leaves on the hull side.
signature_regions.proof_conditions: Seen through the glazing as a line at waist height inside each leaf.
signature_regions.verification: Holding load of a raised rail; trip risk of the recess when lowered.

spatial_topology.description: The passenger hall takes the whole Main deck between the two working ends, on the centreline, inside the Passenger hall interior: the Port gate band on one side, the Starboard gate band on the other and the end bulwarks fore and aft, with the Crew spaces below it inside the hull and the Helm cabin above it on the roof at mid-length. Passengers enter from the pier through whichever gate band lies against it, and the crew stair at mid-length leads down to the crew spaces and up to the helm cabin.
spatial_topology.boundaries: The whole main deck between the two working ends, on the centreline: the port row of gates on one side, the starboard row on the other and the end bulwarks fore and aft, with the crew spaces below it inside the hull and the helm cabin above it on the roof at mid-length.
spatial_topology.connections: The pier through the port gate band or the starboard gate band, whichever side lies against it; the crew spaces below and the helm cabin above through the crew stair at mid-length.
spatial_topology.circulation: Passengers enter and leave through the gates on whichever side lies against the pier and cross the width to the benches. The crew walk along the hall to the mooring stations inside the bulwark at both ends.
spatial_topology.light: Daylight through the glazed upper halves of the gate leaves along both sides; as a proposal, a line of fixed lights runs under the roof along the centreline.

interior.layout: One long open room with nothing dividing it along its length. Cross benches run from the port standing band to the starboard one, each a few steps from a gate, with a clear standing band inside each row of gates. As a proposal, bicycle racks stand against the bulwark at both ends, clear of every gate. The hall is the only place to rest: with the gates closed, passengers sit out of the wind with the harbour in view through the glazed upper halves.
interior.materials: As proposals, plain timber benches on steel frames, a painted steel floor and the underside of the aluminium roof left plain.
interior.fixed_furniture: The cross benches and, as a proposal, the bicycle racks at both ends.
interior.identity: Rows of benches running across the width between two long bands of glazed gates, so the whole room faces the pier side at every stop.
interior.undetermined: The foundation does not decide the standing capacity of the hall.

spatial_topology.description: The helm cabin is the room inside the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, standing on the roof at mid-length on the centreline and bounded by its four glazed walls. It is entered from the hall below through the Helm cabin floor hatch at the head of the crew stair, and from the Roof walkway through the Helm cabin walkway door in its port wall.
spatial_topology.boundaries: The four glazed walls of the helm cabin, standing on the roof at mid-length on the centreline.
spatial_topology.connections: The hall below through the floor hatch and the crew stair; the roof walkway through the port door and the walkway steps.
spatial_topology.circulation: Crew only: up the crew stair through the floor hatch to the two helm consoles, and out to the walkway through the port door.
spatial_topology.light: Daylight through the glazing on all four faces.

interior.layout: One helm console faces each end on the centreline, with a clear floor between them around the hatch.
interior.materials: As proposals, a painted steel floor and painted walls below the glazing.
interior.fixed_furniture: The two helm consoles, one facing each end.
interior.identity: A small glazed room that looks the same toward both ends.
interior.undetermined: The cabin's finishes are not decided beyond the proposals above.

spatial_topology.region: The walkway around the helm cabin
spatial_topology.description: The walkway around the helm cabin lies on the Roof, between the Helm cabin inside and the roof edge outside, open to the sky. The crew reach it from the helm cabin through the Helm cabin walkway door and down the Walkway steps on the port side.
spatial_topology.boundaries: The helm cabin inside, the roof edge outside.
spatial_topology.connections: The helm cabin through its port door and the walkway steps.
spatial_topology.circulation: Crew only, for cleaning the cabin glazing.
spatial_topology.light: Open to the sky; no walkway lighting is decided.

configuration_states.description: The gate leaves of the Port gate band and the Starboard gate band hang between the fixed posts on upper and lower runner tracks. In the standard state every leaf is closed and each side is a glazed wall that cannot be passed. Opened on one side, the leaves of that side unlatch together, slide along the outer track just outside the hull plating toward one end and stack behind a post, leaving that side clear from deck to roof to walk across; the other side stays closed.
configuration_states.fixed_geometry: The posts and the upper and lower runner tracks along each side.
configuration_states.mechanism_location: The outer track just outside the hull plating, under the roof edge and above the sheer; the leaves on one side unlatch together and slide along it.
configuration_states.stowage: Stacked behind a post toward one end.
configuration_states.swept_volume: A narrow band just outside the hull plating along the side.
configuration_states.human_use_by_state: Closed, the side is a glazed wall that cannot be passed; open, the side is clear from deck to roof and can be walked across between the hall and the pier, and the whole hall is aired across its width.

configuration_states.description: The rail sections hang on a lower hinge on each post inside the Port gate band and the Starboard gate band. In the standard state they are raised as a guard line across each side opening that cannot be passed; lowered, each swings through a quarter circle down to the deck edge and folds flat into a recess there, flush with the deck, so the opening can be walked over.
configuration_states.fixed_geometry: The hinge brackets on each post.
configuration_states.mechanism_location: A lower hinge on each post.
configuration_states.stowage: Folded flat into a recess in the deck edge.
configuration_states.swept_volume: A quarter circle inside each opening down to the deck edge, across the standing band beside it, which is kept clear while the rail moves.
configuration_states.human_use_by_state: Raised, it is a guard line across the side opening that cannot be passed; lowered, it lies flush with the deck and can be walked over.

decks.organization: The crew spaces inside the hull, below the hall, reached by the lower flight of the crew stair at mid-length.

decks.name: Main deck
decks.description: The Main deck is the passenger level inside the Hall, level from end to end and a short step above the pier, running between the raked end bulwarks with a gate band along each side.
decks.organization: The hall, level from end to end and a short step above the pier, with the cross benches, a clear standing band inside each row of gates and a mooring station in each corner inside the raked bulwarks.

decks.name: Roof
decks.description: The Roof is the continuous roof over the Hall from end bulwark to end bulwark; only the Roof walkway around the Helm cabin is walked, and only by the crew.
decks.organization: The continuous roof over the hall. Only the walkway around the helm cabin is walked, by the crew, for cleaning the cabin glazing; passengers never go up there.

decks.name: Helm cabin
decks.description: The Helm cabin deck is the floor of the Helm cabin, a step above the roof at mid-length on the centreline, with the hatch over the crew stair.
decks.organization: The helm cabin floor, a step above the roof, with the hatch over the crew stair.

openings.name: Port gate band
openings.description: On the port side of the Hall on the Main deck, the Port gate band is one long opening divided by slim posts and closed by a row of sliding gate leaves, each glazed in its upper half; the leaves slide toward one end on the outer track and stack behind a post. The posts carry the roof loads down into the hull side around each opening.

openings.name: Starboard gate band
openings.description: On the starboard side of the Hall on the Main deck, the Starboard gate band repeats the port band: one long opening divided by slim posts and closed by sliding gate leaves glazed in their upper halves, which slide toward one end on the outer track and stack behind a post, with the posts carrying the roof loads into the hull side.

openings.name: Helm cabin forward glazing
openings.description: Fixed glazing in the forward wall of the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, set in that wall's shallow recess above a solid sill.

openings.name: Helm cabin aft glazing
openings.description: Fixed glazing in the aft wall of the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, set in that wall's shallow recess above a solid sill.

openings.name: Helm cabin port glazing
openings.description: Fixed glazing in the port wall of the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, set in that wall's shallow recess beside the walkway door.

openings.name: Helm cabin starboard glazing
openings.description: Fixed glazing in the starboard wall of the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, set in that wall's shallow recess above a solid sill.

openings.name: Helm cabin floor hatch
openings.description: A hatch in the floor of the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, facing downward over the top of the crew stair, through which the stair rises from the hall floor.

openings.name: Helm cabin walkway door
openings.description: A door in the port wall of the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck that opens onto the roof walkway at the head of the walkway steps.

surfaces.name: Crew floor
surfaces.description: The Crew floor is the floor of the crew spaces on the Crew spaces deck, within the hull below the hall, across the hull's width.

surfaces.name: Hall floor
surfaces.description: The Hall floor is the floor of the Passenger hall interior on the Main deck, level from end to end and a short step above the pier, running between the two gate bands.

surfaces.name: Helm cabin floor
surfaces.description: The Helm cabin floor lies within the Helm cabin on the Helm cabin deck, a step above the roof, with the floor hatch over the crew stair.

surfaces.name: Roof walkway
surfaces.description: The Roof walkway is a narrow walkway on the Roof around the Helm cabin, running between the cabin walls and the roof edge.

routes.name: Crew stair, lower flight
routes.description: The lower flight of the crew stair runs vertically at mid-length inside the hull, from the Crew floor on the Crew spaces deck up to the Hall floor on the Main deck. It passes through no opening and stands within the hull below the hall; its landings are not described.
routes.support: The crew stair at mid-length, inside the hull below the hall.

routes.name: Crew stair, upper flight
routes.description: The upper flight continues the same crew stair vertically at mid-length, from the Hall floor on the Main deck up through the roof to the Helm cabin floor on the Helm cabin deck, arriving through the Helm cabin floor hatch; its landings are not described.
routes.support: The same crew stair rising through the roof to the hatch in the helm cabin floor.

routes.name: Walkway steps
routes.description: The Walkway steps lead to port from the Helm cabin floor on the Helm cabin deck, out through the Helm cabin walkway door and two steps down to the Roof walkway on the Roof, carried on the cabin plinth.
routes.support: Two steps down outside the port door, from the cabin floor to the walkway, carried on the cabin plinth.
